title: macOS: headset power on/off emits spurious play/pause → phantom record toggle
description:
## Summary
On the macOS app, powering the BlueParrott headset OFF or ON spuriously toggles the mic record state. A power transition is misread as a button press.

## Root cause
HeadsetRemoteCommandManager (macOS) holds the Now Playing slot (continuous silent audio, reported `.playing`) and registers MPRemoteCommandCenter play/pause/toggle handlers. When the headset disconnects (power off) macOS sends a `pause` transport command; when it connects (power on) a `play`. `handlePause()` treats ❚❚ as a toggle (intentional for AirPods single-press), and `handlePlay()` starts recording from `.ready` — so each power transition fires `startRecording()`.

This is the unreliable-proxy class of behavior the macOS-BlueParrott-CoreBluetooth epic exists to replace; it is NOT caused by the Phase A2 GATT explorer (which only logs).

## Evidence (logs-20260602-213403.txt)
21:32:36.997 [HeadsetRemote] Headset: ❚❚ received — state=Ready
21:32:37.003 [HeadsetRemote] Headset: recording started
21:32:37.242 [BPExplore]    disconnected: ...device has disconnected from us.
(pause command arrives ~245ms before the BLE disconnect = the power-off.)
No [BluetoothAudio] lines → the CoreAudio mute-proxy/PTT is OFF and is not involved.

## Repro
macOS app, headset control enabled, BlueParrott connected. Toggle the headset power off, then on. Observe record start/stop with no button press.

## Fix options
1. Targeted mitigation: ignore play/pause/toggle MPRemoteCommandCenter commands that arrive within ~1.5s of a BlueParrott BLE connect/disconnect (keeps AirPods PTT working). Add unit tests.
2. Superseded by voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.6 (rewire macOS to drive BlueParrottBLEManager GATT button events and retire the media-key/mute proxies as the BlueParrott trigger).

## Caveat
A naive 'don't start recording on pause' breaks AirPods PTT, which relies on the ❚❚-as-toggle behavior. Any fix must preserve that.

## Acceptance
Powering the BlueParrott headset off/on does NOT change record state on macOS; AirPods single-press PTT still works.
close_reason: Folded into voice-code-macos-headset-loop-state-machine-3x1 — the SessionReducer media-key handling + keep-alive gating addresses the power-transition phantom toggle (the unreliable-proxy class this overhaul replaces).

title: BlueParrott BLE silently never connects when headset is HFP-bonded but not advertising — add scan-timeout re-probe
description:
## Problem
On macOS the BlueParrott button is sometimes completely dead for an entire session: no button events, recording never triggers from the headset. The headset is connected for AUDIO (HFP) the whole time, but the BLE control service never connects, so no gestures are delivered.

## Evidence (macOS logs 2026-06-03 15:41–15:44, voice-code build with capture observability)
```
15:41:54.747  BlueParrottBLE: start
15:41:55.203  BlueParrottBLE: Bluetooth powered on → scheduling scan (attempt 1)
15:41:56.246  BlueParrottBLE: scanning for advertised service
15:41:56.246  BlueParrottBLE: scanning… (attempt 1)
              … no further BlueParrottBLE lines all session. No "connected", no button DOWN/UP.
15:43:57.646  VoiceInput: input device=B450-XT II v1.08 [uid=3C-68-16-60-A8-1E:input] 16000Hz   ← headset IS connected for HFP audio
```
The two recordings in that session came from the on-screen mic button, not the headset.

## Root cause
`CBCentralAdapter.scanForButtonService()` tries `retrieveConnectedPeripherals(withServices:[service])` ONCE, then falls back to `scanForPeripherals(withServices:[service])`. Once the headset is bonded for HFP it frequently is NOT advertising the GATT control service (design Risk #3), so the scan never gets a `didDiscover` callback. Crucially, the manager's retry path (`bleDidFailToConnect` → `scheduleConnect`) only fires on a failed *connect attempt* — a fruitless *scan* produces no callback, so nothing re-arms. The manager scans forever and the button stays dead until the app is relaunched at a moment the device happens to be discoverable.

See `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift`:
- `scheduleConnect()` (~190): schedules one scan, no timeout.
- `CBCentralAdapter.scanForButtonService()` (~370): retrieveConnectedPeripherals once, else scanForPeripherals.

## Technical approach
Add a **scan-timeout re-probe** so an unfruitful scan is treated like a transient failure and retried (re-running retrieveConnectedPeripherals each time, which picks up a headset that became BLE-available after the first scan):

1. In `scheduleConnect()`, when the scan work runs, also arm a `scanTimeout` work item (e.g. ~8–10s). If it fires while still `enabled && !isConnected`, stop the scan and route through the existing backoff: bump `retryCount`/`inSlowRetry` and call `scheduleConnect()` again (fast retries → infinite 30s slow-retry, mirroring the connect-failure path). Each re-attempt re-runs `scanForButtonService()`, so `retrieveConnectedPeripherals` is re-checked every cycle.
2. Cancel the scan-timeout on `bleDidConnect`/`bleDidFailToConnect`/`stop`.
3. `CBCentralAdapter.scanForButtonService()` should `stopScan()` before re-scanning to avoid stacking scans.
4. (Optional, stronger) Also keep periodically calling `retrieveConnectedPeripherals` independent of advertising — that is the reliable path for an HFP-bonded device.

All of this is unit-testable through the existing `BLECentral` seam + synchronous `scheduleWork`: drive a scan that never yields a connect and assert another `scanForButtonService()` attempt is made after the timeout, and that it escalates to slow-retry rather than going silent.

## Acceptance criteria
- A headset that is HFP-connected but not advertising at launch still gets its BLE button connected within a bounded time (re-probe loop, not a one-shot scan).
- A scan that finds nothing escalates through the existing fast→slow retry backoff instead of going silent forever.
- Logs show the re-probe attempts (no silent dead state).
- Unit tests: fruitless-scan → re-probe scheduled; escalation to slow-retry; timeout cancelled on connect/stop. macOS + iOS suites still pass (`make test-mac`, `make test`).

## Scope
macOS BlueParrott BLE path only. Discovered during b4i.8 manual hardware validation; blocks completing that validation (button can't be exercised when BLE never connects). Separate from the audio capture warm-up bug (voice-code-headset-hfp-mic-warmup-66p).

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Opus design consult + plan refinement (2026-06-03).

DIAGNOSIS confirmed: retrieveConnectedPeripherals returns empty because HFP (classic BR/EDR) is a separate link from BLE GATT — legit. Connects happen only via scan catching an infrequent advertisement (~50s first-connect).

STEP A (DONE, unit-tested): continuous scan. Was stop(8s)->gap(2s)->rescan, which has blind spots that miss the BlueParrott's infrequent adverts. Now: scanForButtonService starts ONE scan and leaves it running (guard !manager.isScanning); the scan-timeout tick no longer stops the scan — it only re-checks the already-connected fast path + backs off cadence/logging. BlueParrottBLEManagerTests 32/32.

STEP B (TODO): identifier-based reconnect, with the consult's critical correction:
- DO persist peripheral.identifier (UserDefaults) on didConnect; on launch use retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:)+connect().
- CRITICAL HOLE in the naive version: connect() has NO timeout; firing bleDidStartConnecting (which cancels the scan-timeout) on a STALE id => hangs forever, button dead until restart (worse than 50s). 
  FIX: split adapter connect — advert/already-connected connect (fast, cancels scan-timeout) vs connectKnown(identifier:) under a SEPARATE connect-watchdog that does NOT get cancelled by bleDidStartConnecting. Watchdog trip => cancelPeripheralConnection + fall back to scan; clear saved id after repeated failures (stale-id hygiene); gate on .poweredOn.
- The real 'near-instant' reconnect = on didDisconnect, re-issue connect() to the HELD CBPeripheral (no/long timeout is correct there), NOT the cold-launch path.
- SKIP CB state restoration on macOS (iOS-background feature).
- ADD post-connect discovery watchdog: connected but never isNotifying within N s => treat as failed + re-probe.
- Validate via BLECentral seam (add connectKnown/retrieveKnown + watchdog on injected scheduleWork, copy scanTimeoutGeneration guard).

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text: STEP A hardware result (logs-20260603-200451): continuous scan works as designed — single 'scanning for advertised service (continuous)' line, no restart churn across re-probe cycles (confirmed: subsequent attempts log only 'scanning… (attempt N)', adapter did not restart). BUT first-connect was still ~41s (start 20:03:14 → connected 20:03:55), only marginally better than the prior ~53s. Conclusion: the gaps were NOT the main cause — the BlueParrott advertises its control service rarely. So Step A is a minor win; STEP B (identifier-based reconnect with the connect-watchdog/stale-id fix) is required for fast connect. Proceeding to B.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
STEP B implemented + unit-tested (BlueParrottBLEManager.swift, macOS path).

Manager (testable via BLECentral seam):
- attemptConnect(): prefer a direct connect to the persisted 'known' peripheral before scanning. hasKnownPeripheral gate + knownConnectAttempts budget.
- connect-watchdog (connectTimeout=8s): SEPARATE from scan-timeout, generation-guarded, NOT cancelled by bleDidStartConnecting — the stale-id hang guard. Trip => cancelConnection + escalateAndReconnect; after maxKnownConnectAttempts(=2) => forgetKnownPeripheral and fall back to scan.
- discovery-watchdog (discoveryTimeout=5s): armed on bleDidConnect; cancelled by new bleDidStartNotifying callback; trip => tear down half-open link (isConnected=false) + re-probe.
- bleDidFailToConnect routes a known-connect-in-flight through the stale-id budget; stop()/poweredOff/resetting/disconnect cancel both watchdogs.

Adapter (CoreBluetooth, not unit-tested): persist peripheral.identifier to UserDefaults on didConnect; connectKnownPeripheral()=retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:)+connect WITHOUT firing bleDidStartConnecting; forgetKnownPeripheral(); bleDidStartNotifying fired from didUpdateNotificationStateFor; held-peripheral warm reconnect on unexpected didDisconnect (intentionalDisconnect guard). Skipped CB state restoration (iOS-only).

Tests: 11 new cases; BlueParrottBLEManagerTests 43/43. macOS unit bundle 1096 tests 0 failures; iOS 1008 unit + UI 0 failures (make non-zero exit = pre-existing AudioUnit crash-handler host crash in VoiceInputManager, not an assertion failure). Not committed — code review next.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Code-review fixes applied (STEP B):

#1 (real-adapter half-open reconnect-loop without backoff): the discovery-watchdog teardown now drives an ESCALATING re-probe off a new discoveryFailures counter that survives connect cycles (bleDidConnect no longer resets the half-open backoff; only markNotificationsLive / stop / reconnect / genuine disconnect clear it). A persistently half-open headset now escalates fast→slow (slowRetryDelay) instead of looping every ~6s. Added teardownInProgress flag so the teardown-induced didDisconnect doesn't reset counters or double-schedule (the watchdog owns the re-probe). New test testRepeatedDiscoveryFailures_backOffToSlowReprobe.

#3 (intentionalDisconnect could latch true with no matching didDisconnect): adapter now clears it on every fresh connect (connect/connectKnown), bounding the flag.

#5 (discovery watchdog not cancelled by an incoming button value): bleDidUpdateButtonValue now clears a pending discovery watchdog (a real gesture proves notifications flow). markNotificationsLive() shared by bleDidStartNotifying + value path. New tests testButtonValue_cancelsDiscoveryWatchdog, testNotificationsLive_clearsDiscoveryFailureBackoff.

#2 (held-reconnect 'indefinitely-pending' comment overstated): corrected the adapter comment to describe the actual bounded behavior (warm reconnect is a head start for quick returns; the manager's known-connect watchdog bounds longer absences). Behavior unchanged.

#4 (no adapter unit coverage): inherent to the un-testable CBCentralAdapter (the BLECentral seam exists for this) — accepted, consistent with existing untested adapter code.

Tests: BlueParrottBLEManagerTests 46/46 (43 + 3 new). Full macOS unit bundle 1096 tests, 1 skipped, 0 failures, 0 failed cases. iOS unaffected (all edits macOS-gated; BLE test file excluded from iOS target). Not committed.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Review-fix round 2 applied:

#1 (priority — teardownInProgress coordination was untested): added 2 tests driving the real-adapter callback ordering the fake can't auto-produce — testTeardownDisconnect_doesNotDoubleScheduleOrResetBackoff (a teardown-induced bleDidDisconnect after a discovery trip must NOT double-schedule or reset discoveryFailures; the watchdog's re-probe is the sole re-arm) and testGenuineDisconnect_afterHalfOpen_resetsBackoffAndReArms (a genuine disconnect, flag already cleared, DOES reset the backoff + re-arm). Locks down the suppression branch.

#2 (held-reconnect bypassed connectKnown): didDisconnect's warm reconnect now routes through connectKnown(to:) instead of a raw manager.connect, so the stale per-session characteristic cache (buttonChar/modeChar/appNameChar) is dropped on reconnect rather than relying on re-discovery to paper over a setNotifyValue on an invalid characteristic.

#3 (start() asymmetry): start() now resets knownConnectAttempts/discoveryFailures/teardownInProgress too (was only retryCount/inSlowRetry). Safe before; symmetric now.

#4 (late-didDisconnect theoretical hazard): noted only, inherent CoreBluetooth limitation, not actionable.

Tests: BlueParrottBLEManagerTests 48/48 (** TEST SUCCEEDED **). Full macOS unit bundle: 0 failed cases / 0 errors, all 48 BLE tests run inside it. iOS unaffected (all edits macOS-gated). Not committed.

title: Speech capture intermittently records silence — use headset HFP mic with SCO warm-up, not built-in mic
description:
## Problem
Speech capture intermittently records silence — SFSpeechRecognizer ends with "No speech detected" even on genuine multi-second recordings. Major real-world impact: when driving with the phone mounted on the dash, the mic captures poorly because the app records from the phone's BUILT-IN mic (across the car) instead of the headset mic near the user's mouth.

## Root cause
Two related issues:

1. **iOS deliberately forces the built-in device mic** and avoids the Bluetooth HFP mic. See `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/VoiceInputManager.swift` (~line 131): "No .allowBluetooth — that forces AirPods into HFP mode which breaks MPRemoteCommandCenter stem-press delivery. Device mic is used instead, which gives better quality than HFP's 16kHz anyway." That assumption only holds when the phone is near the mouth. Phone-on-dash + headset-on-ear = built-in mic is across the car → poor capture. This is the driving bug.

2. **HFP/SCO warm-up dead zone.** When the headset HFP mic IS the route (macOS, route=16000Hz), the SCO link is slow to start delivering audio — the first chunk (up to seconds) is silence. Short recordings land entirely in that dead window → "No speech detected". macOS has no input-device selection at all (`AVAudioEngine` uses the system default input, which auto-switches to the connected headset).

## Evidence (macOS logs 2026-06-03)
- 3.7s genuine button hold → "No speech detected" (route 16000Hz / HFP)
- 19.4s hold → captured full message (HFP warmed up by then)
- UI-triggered recordings (no headset button involved) failed the same way → NOT specific to the BlueParrott button. Button PTT path (down→record, up→send) is functioning.

## Correct fix direction
Use the HEADSET (HFP) mic and make it reliable — the user wants the mic near their mouth, especially while driving. Do NOT "fix" this by switching to the built-in mic.
- Warm up / wait for the SCO route to settle before starting SFSpeechRecognizer (pre-roll, or gate recognition on first non-silent buffers / route-ready).
- Reconsider the iOS `.allowBluetooth` decision so the headset mic can be selected when a headset is the intended input (without losing MPRemoteCommandCenter stem-press delivery — that interaction is the original reason it was disabled and must be preserved/retested).
- macOS: add explicit input-device handling; log the actual input device (name + UID), not just sample rate, to confirm which mic is live.

## Scope / platforms
Cross-platform (iOS + macOS). Separate from the BlueParrott BLE button work (task voice-code-macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth-b4i.8) — the button is fine; this is the audio-capture layer.

## Acceptance
- A short (~2-3s) hold reliably captures speech via the headset mic (no silent dead zone).
- Driving scenario (phone on dash, headset worn) captures from the headset mic, not the phone's built-in mic.
- MPRemoteCommandCenter stem-press delivery still works on iOS (no regression from any .allowBluetooth change).
- Tests around the device-selection / warm-up logic.
close_reason: Implemented validated F2 (keep-alive suspend gated to BLE path) + F3 (zero-buffer warm-up watchdog with one-shot restart, generation-token guarded). Tests pass iOS+macOS (0 failures). iOS .allowBluetooth mic-switch deliberately deferred per bug evidence (dead zone not mic-specific; stem-press risk) — see prior comment.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text: Hardware evidence (logs-20260603-161342, cims-jb7-docker working dir): the warm-up dead zone is NOT Bluetooth/HFP-specific. Built-in MacBook mic: 'MacBook Pro Microphone 48000Hz … firstAudio=3.56s silent=95% peak=0.0137' -> No speech. Headset HFP mic, same session: 'B450-XT II 16000Hz … firstAudio=1.23s silent=71% peak=0.0502' -> captured fine. The built-in mic dead zone (3.56s) is LONGER than the HFP mic (1.23s). Conclusion: do NOT fix this by switching to the built-in mic — it is equally/more affected. Fix is warm-up handling (gate recognition until the input route delivers non-silent buffers), independent of mic. Verify any fix against the capture-summary firstAudio offset.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Hardware result (logs-20260603-200451): suspending the keep-alive during recording CUT the warm-up dead zone roughly in half on the HFP mic — firstAudio 1.23s → 0.63s, peak 0.2655, silent 52% (was 71%); 'Testing 123' captured + sent. So the continuously-playing silent keep-alive output WAS a real contributor to the dead zone. Experiment validated; next: gate the suspend to the BLE-button path (don't regress macOS AirPods stop-during-recording) and keep the firstAudio metric.

NEW, distinct issue surfaced: the FIRST recording right after BLE connect got ZERO buffers (buffers=0 frames=0 firstAudio=never → No speech) over a 4.7s hold; the very next press worked (0.63s). This is total route-dead on first capture (not silent buffers) — the macOS analog of the known iOS 'engine starts without producing buffers after a transition' issue (see VoiceInputManager iOS comment). Fix candidates: warm the AVAudioEngine / wait for the input route to be live before first capture, or detect buffers=0 and auto-restart the capture once.

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
Implemented validated, testable core (F2 + F3) per the hardware evidence and bug comments.

F2 — keep-alive suspend now GATED to the BlueParrott BLE button path (was unconditional on macOS). New RecordingTrigger (mediaKey|blueParrott) threaded through startRecording(trigger:); HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.shouldSuspendKeepAlive(trigger:) is true only for .blueParrott. BLE events arrive over CoreBluetooth (not MPRemoteCommandCenter), so dropping Now-Playing during capture costs nothing and halves the dead zone (1.23s->0.63s). AirPods/media-key path no longer suspends -> keeps Now-Playing so a second stem press stops recording (no regression).

F3 — zero-buffer warm-up watchdog in VoiceInputManager. After engine start a watchdog (0.6s, injectable seam) checks the capture monitor; ZERO buffers = route never went live -> restart capture ONCE, reusing the recognition request. Silent-but-present buffers are NOT restarted (that is the F2 dead zone). Engine setup refactored into startCaptureEngine() shared by start+restart. Pure decision RecordingWarmup.shouldRestartCapture(bufferCount:alreadyRestarted:).

Tests: 9 new (6 in VoiceInputManagerTests, 4 in HeadsetRemoteCommandManagerTests incl. pure decisions). iOS make test SUCCEEDED 0 failures; macOS bundle 1095 tests 0 failures. macOS Error 65 is the pre-existing headless-host crash flake in testBlueParrottBLE_pttHold_... (a test I did not touch).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the iOS .allowBluetooth mic-switch. Bug comments conclude the dead zone is NOT mic-specific (built-in is equally/worse affected) and warn the change risks the MPRemoteCommandCenter stem-press path, unverifiable headless. Left iOS audio-session config untouched; warm-up handling is the validated fix. Flag for hardware retest if mic-source policy is revisited.

title: macOS BlueParrott button via CoreBluetooth
description:
## Design Document
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md

## Overview
Detect BlueParrott multifunction-button events on macOS by reimplementing the
iOS BPHeadset SDK's BLE GATT integration directly on CoreBluetooth, since the
SDK xcframework ships iOS-only slices. Replaces the current (broken) CoreAudio
mute-proxy trigger that never sees the button.

- Phase A: a DEBUG-only collector that captures the proprietary GATT protocol
  (characteristic UUIDs, App-Mode enable handshake, button-event byte format) by
  instrumenting the working iOS SDK, plus an App-Mode persistence experiment
  that decides Phase B's scope.
- Phase B: a macOS CoreBluetooth client + pure byte parser feeding the existing
  BlueParrottButtonDelegate / HeadsetRemoteCommandManager state machine unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. macOS button down starts recording and up stops+sends, matching iOS PTT behavior.
2. macOS tap / double-tap / long-press map to the same actions as iOS
   (HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift:626-665).
3. BlueParrottEventParser unit tests pass against the captured real-device byte
   sequences for all five gestures, and return nil for empty/unknown payloads.
4. Connect/retry/re-arm unit tests pass with a faked BLECentral (no hardware).
5. Out-of-range disconnect returns the state machine to ready and reconnects
   automatically when the headset returns.
6. make build-mac (scheme VoiceCodeMac) succeeds with
   com.apple.security.device.bluetooth added; make build (iOS) is unchanged.
7. The Phase A collector (BPSniffer) is absent from release builds
   (#if DEBUG verified by a release-config build).
8. make test-mac passes (runs the new macOS VoiceCodeMacTests) and make test
   still passes (iOS suite, no regression).
close_reason: Superseded by voice-code-macos-headset-loop-state-machine-3x1; the macOS CoreBluetooth button work is folded into the overhaul epic.

title: Build Phase A1 DEBUG GATT collector (BPSniffer) to capture the BlueParrott protocol
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-blueparrott-corebluetooth.md#3-detailed-design (Phase A1 — passive observer)

## Context
Unblocking step. The proprietary GATT protocol (characteristic UUIDs, App-Mode enable handshake, per-gesture byte format) is not in the public SDK header — capture it by instrumenting the working iOS BPHeadset SDK.

## Requirements
- [ ] New `BPSniffer.swift`, gated `#if DEBUG && os(iOS)`
- [ ] Swizzle `CBPeripheral.writeValue(_:for:type:)` → log characteristic UUID + payload hex
- [ ] Discover the SDK's peripheral delegate at runtime and swizzle `peripheral:didUpdateValueForCharacteristic:` → log UUID + value hex
- [ ] Route all output through `LogManager.shared.log(category: "BPSniff")`
- [ ] Install the hook from a DEBUG entry point when BlueParrott is enabled
- [ ] On hardware: capture the App-Mode enable write (char + bytes) and each gesture's notification (char + bytes) for down/up/tap/double-tap/long-press

## Technical Approach
Per the doc's Code Examples (BPSniffer). Objective-C runtime method swizzling.
- New files: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BPSniffer.swift`
- Dependencies: none (iOS already has the BLE entitlement and links the working SDK)

## Verification
- [ ] Manual (hardware): iOS DEBUG build, enable BlueParrott, press all 5 gestures → "BPSniff" logs show the enable-write and per-gesture bytes
- [ ] Release-config build confirms `BPSniffer` is compiled out

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #7 (collector absent from release builds); produces the captured bytes that epic #3 depends on.

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: "Add macOS Bluetooth entitlement and usage description".

description:

comments.author: travisbrown
comments.text:
A2 GATT explorer built, made runnable on macOS, and unit-tested.

Done (automatable):
- New BPGattExplorer.swift (#if DEBUG, cross-platform): standalone CBCentralManager client that scans service 95665a00-…, enumerates services/characteristics + properties, subscribes to every notifier, and logs notification hex via LogManager category "BPExplore". Prefers retrieveConnectedPeripherals (headset bonded for HFP may not advertise) then falls back to scanning. Handles all CBManagerState cases incl. .unauthorized.

title: macOS headset hands-free loop — state-machine overhaul
description:
## Design Document
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md
(companion findings/evidence: @docs/design/macos-headset-loop-findings.md)

## Overview
Re-model the macOS BlueParrott/headset hands-free loop (button → record →
transcribe → send → hear response → idle) as two pure, unit-testable reducers
with thin effect executors, replacing the implicit state guards in
HeadsetRemoteCommandManager + BlueParrottPTTArbitrator. This eliminates the
strand/misfire bugs found during hardware testing:

- **Connection machine** (BLEConnReducer): continuous scan; identifier-based
  reconnect with a connect-watchdog (no stale-id hang) + immediate fall-to-scan
  on empty retrieve; held-peripheral reconnect on disconnect; discovery watchdog.
- **Interaction machine** (SessionReducer: idle/recording/finalizing/
  awaitingResponse/speaking): a fallback/interrupt/timeout edge out of every busy
  state so nothing strands — fixes the `.sending` ("Processing") strand and adds a
  `.recording` safety net (captureEnded) for recognizer auto-finalize / disconnect
  mid-record.
- **Gesture de-bracketer** (BlueParrottGestureRecognizer): hold = PTT, tap =
  toggle, double-tap = interrupt, plus hold/tap barge-in during speaking/awaiting.
- **Capture-readiness** recovery (zero-buffer first capture) and **BLE-gated
  keep-alive** suspension (mic warm-up).

Scope: macOS adopts the new reducers; iOS keeps its existing BPHeadset/HeadsetState
path (reducer core designed to be reusable by iOS later). No backend/protocol
changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
(from the design doc §4)
1. After a successful utterance whose prompt produces NO spoken response, the
   button records again within the await timeout (no permanent strand). [F4]
2. A tap/double-tap during speaking/awaitingResponse interrupts/dismisses to idle;
   a HOLD during either state barges in (interrupt + start a new recording in one
   gesture). [F4/F5]
3. The first capture after BLE connect that yields zero buffers auto-restarts once
   and captures on the retry (no user re-press). [F3]
4. A held press records and release sends (PTT); a quick tap latches recording and
   a second tap sends (toggle) — no record/stop flicker on tap. [F5]
5. With a saved peripheral id, reconnect after relaunch or an out-of-range
   round-trip completes without waiting for an advertisement; a stale id never
   hangs the button (falls back to scan within the connect watchdog). [F1]
6. SessionReducer/ConnReducer/BlueParrottGestureRecognizer unit tests pass and the
   reducers contain no I/O; `make test-mac-unit` and `make test` are green.
7. The macOS AirPods path is unaffected: a mediaKey-sourced recording does NOT
   suspend the keep-alive, and play/pause stem presses still start/stop recording.
8. `.recording` cannot strand: if capture ends with no `up` (recognizer silence
   auto-finalize or headset disconnect mid-recording) the machine finalizes
   (sends if non-empty, else returns to idle). [Goal #2]

## Related bugs (folded into this overhaul)
- voice-code-blueparrott-ble-scan-timeout-ghw (F1 — discovery/reconnect)
- voice-code-headset-hfp-mic-warmup-66p (F2/F3 — warm-up / zero-buffer capture)

## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#gesture-recognizer-de-bracketer

## Context
The raw GATT stream brackets every gesture with down/up (tap=01,00,02; double=01,00,01,00,03; hold=01,04,00). Driving the state machine off raw down/up flickers on taps. This pure recognizer converts raw signals into exactly one semantic gesture per physical action, replacing the retired BlueParrottPTTArbitrator. Foundation for the session executor.

## Requirements
- [ ] `RawButtonSignal` enum: down, up, tapCode, doubleTapCode, longPressCode
- [ ] `HeadsetGesture` enum: holdStarted, holdEnded, tap, doubleTap (NO longPress — a hold is PTT; 04 is ignored)
- [ ] `BlueParrottGestureRecognizer`: `feed(_:)`; hold-timer (holdThreshold=0.30) + per-press `generation` + `isDown` guard so a fast double-tap can't trip a stale hold timer
- [ ] Discrete tap/double from the hardware 02/03 codes; longPressCode ignored (in-bracket)
- [ ] scheduler-injected (`scheduleAfter`), reads no wall-clock

## Technical Approach
- New file: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottGestureRecognizer.swift` (cross-platform; pure logic)
- Dependencies: none (parallel foundation)

## Verification

Epic #4 (PTT/tap, no flicker), part of #2 (gesture set) and #6 (unit tests, no I/O).

title: Implement SessionReducer (interaction state machine)
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#interaction-session-machine

## Context
The implicit HeadsetState guards strand in `.sending` ("Processing") and have no barge-in. This pure reducer models the interaction loop with a fallback/interrupt/timeout edge out of every busy state so nothing strands.

## Requirements
- [ ] `SessionState`: idle, recording, finalizing, awaitingResponse, speaking
- [ ] `SessionEvent`: holdStarted, holdEnded, tap, doubleTap, captureProducedAudio, captureStalled, captureEnded, transcription(String?), ttsStarted, ttsEnded, awaitTimedOut, backendUnavailable
- [ ] `SessionEffect`: startCapture, restartCapture, stopCapture, sendPrompt(String), interruptTTS, suspendKeepAlive, resumeKeepAlive, armTimer/cancelTimer(SessionTimer), updateNowPlaying, log(String); `SessionTimer`: captureGrace, awaitResponse
- [ ] `ButtonSource`: blueParrottBLE, mediaKey, iosSDK
- [ ] Pure `SessionReducer.reduce(state, event, source) -> (state, [effect])`, no I/O
- [ ] Edges: idle+holdStarted/tap→recording; recording+holdEnded/tap/captureEnded→finalizing; recording+captureStalled→restartCapture (once); recording+captureProducedAudio→cancel grace; finalizing+transcription→awaitingResponse(send) or idle; awaitingResponse+awaitTimedOut/backendUnavailable→idle (do NOT cancel prompt); awaitingResponse/speaking +tap/doubleTap→idle (dismiss); +holdStarted→recording (barge-in); idle/awaitingResponse+ttsStarted→speaking; speaking+ttsEnded→idle
- [ ] `suspendKeepAlive` only when source == .blueParrottBLE

## Technical Approach
- New file: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/HeadsetSessionReducer.swift` (cross-platform; pure)
- Dependencies: none (parallel foundation)

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests (cross-platform): awaitTimedOut→idle without cancelling prompt; speaking+tap→idle+interruptTTS; speaking+holdStarted→recording+interruptTTS+startCapture; awaitingResponse+tap→idle; recording+captureStalled→restartCapture; recording+captureEnded→finalizing; idle+ttsStarted→speaking; keep-alive suspend gated to BLE source
- [ ] `make test-mac-unit` and `make test` green

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #1 (F4 strand), #2 (barge-in), #3 (capture restart), #7 (keep-alive gating), #8 (recording no-strand), #6 (unit tests, no I/O).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: Gesture recognizer, Connection reducer, AppSettings persistence, VoiceInput capture-readiness.

title: Implement ConnReducer (BLE connection state machine)
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#connection-machine

## Context
First-connect takes ~41–53s because retrieveConnectedPeripherals is always empty (HFP ≠ BLE GATT) and the headset advertises the control service rarely. This pure reducer models the connection lifecycle with continuous scan + identifier reconnect + watchdogs so connect is fast and never hangs.

## Requirements
- [ ] `BLEConnState`: stopped, unavailable(CBManagerState), scanning(attempt), connecting(ConnectMode), discovering, live, reconnecting; `ConnectMode`: advertised, known
- [ ] `BLEConnEvent`: start, stop, managerState, knownPeripheralResolved, knownPeripheralUnresolved, advertisementDiscovered, connected, connectFailed(retryable), subscribed, scanTick, connectWatchdog, discoveryWatchdog, disconnected
- [ ] `BLEConnEffect`: startContinuousScan, stopScan, resolveKnownPeripheral(UUID), connectAdvertised, connectKnown, reconnectHeld, cancelConnection, discoverAndSubscribe, persistIdentifier, clearSavedIdentifier, armTimer/cancelTimer(BLETimer), log; `BLETimer`: scanTick, connectWatchdog, discoveryWatchdog
- [ ] Pure `ConnReducer.reduce(state, event, savedID:) -> (state, [effect])`, no I/O
- [ ] Key edges: powered-on → known-id resolve (connectWatchdog) else continuous scan; knownPeripheralUnresolved → clear id + scan immediately; connectWatchdog (known) → cancel + clear id + scan; scanTick → re-arm WITHOUT stopScan (continuous); advertisementDiscovered → connect(advertised) + armTimer(connectWatchdog); connecting+connected → discovering + discoveryWatchdog; subscribed → live + persistIdentifier; discoveryWatchdog → scan; live+disconnected → reconnecting(reconnectHeld); connectFailed(either mode) → scan/unavailable

## Technical Approach
- New file: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BLEConnReducer.swift` (cross-platform; pure; imports CoreBluetooth for CBManagerState)
- Dependencies: none (parallel foundation)

## Verification
- [ ] Unit tests (cross-platform): connectWatchdog(known)→scanning+cancelConnection+clearSavedIdentifier; scanTick does NOT emit stopScan; knownPeripheralUnresolved→scanning+clearSavedIdentifier+cancelTimer(connectWatchdog); advertised connect armed+recovers to scan; live+disconnected→reconnecting+reconnectHeld (not connectKnown); subscribed→persistIdentifier
- [ ] `make test-mac-unit` and `make test` green

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #5 (identifier reconnect, watchdogs, no stale-id hang), #6 (unit tests, no I/O).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: Gesture recognizer, Session reducer, AppSettings persistence, VoiceInput capture-readiness.

## Context

title: Add capture-readiness hooks to VoiceInputManager (live buffer signal + restart)
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#detailed-design (F3 capture readiness; see findings F3)

## Context
The first capture right after BLE connect can return ZERO buffers (dead route) → "No speech"; the next press works. The session executor needs live signals to detect this and auto-restart once. Today `AudioCaptureMonitor` only snapshots a summary at stop — it must also signal in-flight.

## Requirements
- [ ] Live callback when the FIRST non-silent buffer arrives (→ feeds session `captureProducedAudio`)
- [ ] A way for the session executor's `captureGrace` timer to detect ZERO buffers (→ feeds `captureStalled`)
- [ ] `restartCapture` entry point: tear down + recreate the AVAudioEngine/recognition mid-recording WITHOUT changing session state (idempotent `stopCapture` semantics preserved)
- [ ] Keep the existing `capture summary firstAudio=…` observability

## Technical Approach
- Modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/VoiceInputManager.swift` (extend `AudioCaptureMonitor`/tap to emit live first-audio + expose buffer count; add restart entry point)
- Dependencies: none (parallel foundation); consumed by the Headset session executor task

## Verification
- [ ] Unit test for any pure piece (e.g., first-non-silent detection on the existing AudioCaptureStats; buffer-count exposure)
- [ ] Manual (hardware, in the executor task): zero-buffer first capture auto-restarts and captures on retry
- [ ] `make test-mac-unit` and `make test` green

## Acceptance Criteria
Supports Epic #3 (zero-buffer auto-restart) and #8 (capture safety net).

## Parallelization
Can be worked alongside: Gesture recognizer, Session reducer, Connection reducer, AppSettings persistence.

title: Wire BlueParrottBLEManager to ConnReducer + add BLECentral seam (connectKnown/reconnectHeld/watchdogs)
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#api-design (BLECentral seam additions) + #connection-reducer--happy-path-identifier-reconnect-watchdogs + #executor-wiring

## Context
Drive BlueParrottBLEManager from the pure ConnReducer via a thin effect executor, and extend the CoreBluetooth seam so the identifier-reconnect + watchdog effects can run. Improves first-connect latency and removes the silent-hang / stale-id failure modes.

## Requirements
- [ ] ConnReducer effect executor in BlueParrottBLEManager (apply effects → CoreBluetooth I/O; feed callbacks back as BLEConnEvents)
- [ ] `BLECentral` additions: `resolveKnownPeripheral(_ id: UUID)` (retrievePeripherals(withIdentifiers:); fires resolved/no-known), `connectKnown()`, `reconnectHeld()`
- [ ] `BLECentralEvents` additions: `bleKnownPeripheralResolved` → knownPeripheralResolved, `bleNoKnownPeripheral` → knownPeripheralUnresolved
- [ ] `connectWatchdog` (advertised ~6s / known ~10s) + `discoveryWatchdog` (~5s) + `scanTick` (~8s) timers via injected `scheduleWork`, generation-guard (mirror `scanTimeoutGeneration`)
- [ ] Persist `peripheral.identifier` on `subscribed` (reads from the retained CBPeripheral); clear on `clearSavedIdentifier`
- [ ] Continuous scan (do not stop/restart between ticks) — keep the existing behavior
- [ ] `CBCentralAdapter` implements the new methods; `FakeBLECentral` extended for tests; emit RawButtonSignal from the parser output for the recognizer (consumed by the headset executor task)

## Technical Approach
- Modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/BlueParrottBLEManager.swift`
- Dependencies: ConnReducer (3x1.3), AppSettings persistence (3x1.4)

## Verification
- [ ] Integration tests (macOS, faked BLECentral + synchronous scheduleWork): saved-id → resolve → connectKnown → connected → live (persistIdentifier); stale id → connectWatchdog → clear + scan; empty retrieve → clear + scan immediately; disconnect → reconnectHeld; discovery stall → re-probe
- [ ] `make test-mac-unit` green; `make test` no iOS regression

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #5 (identifier reconnect, watchdogs, no stale-id hang).

## Parallelization
After ConnReducer + AppSettings persistence land. Can be worked alongside the Headset session executor's non-BLE parts.

title: Wire HeadsetRemoteCommandManager to SessionReducer; retire HeadsetState/arbitrator
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#executor-wiring (event sources, threading & gating) + #session-reducer--strand-proof-barge-in-capture-readiness

## Context
Drive the macOS interaction loop from the pure SessionReducer via a thin executor, replacing the implicit HeadsetState guards and the BlueParrottPTTArbitrator. This is where the strand fixes, barge-in, capture-readiness, and keep-alive gating become live behavior.

## Requirements
- [ ] SessionReducer effect executor in HeadsetRemoteCommandManager (apply effects; main-queue serialized)
- [ ] Wire BlueParrottGestureRecognizer: BLE RawButtonSignal → HeadsetGesture → SessionEvent; mediaKey source maps togglePlayPause/play/pause→tap, nextTrack→doubleTap (source: .mediaKey)
- [ ] Event sources: `voiceInput.$isRecording→false` AND bleDidDisconnect-while-recording → `captureEnded`; executor ALWAYS emits `transcription(_)` after stopCapture (nil on error); `voiceOutput.$isSpeaking`→ttsStarted/ttsEnded; `awaitResponse` timer→awaitTimedOut; client disconnect→backendUnavailable; captureGrace→captureStalled/captureProducedAudio (from VoiceInput hooks)
- [ ] `restartCapture` effect → VoiceInput restart (once per recording)
- [ ] Keep-alive suspend ONLY on source == .blueParrottBLE
- [ ] Gating at executor input: when not engaged (headsetModeEnabled/blueParrottEnabled/stateMachineEngaged) drop gesture/session events, forward only lifecycle
- [ ] Retire `HeadsetState` guards + `BlueParrottPTTArbitrator` on macOS; iOS keeps its existing BPHeadset/HeadsetState path (platform-gate the shared file)

## Technical Approach
- Modify: `ios/VoiceCode/Managers/HeadsetRemoteCommandManager.swift` (+ delete/retire `BlueParrottPTTArbitrator`)
- Dependencies: Gesture recognizer (3x1.1), Session reducer (3x1.2), VoiceInput capture-readiness (3x1.5), BLE conn executor (3x1.6 — provides RawButtonSignal + live BLE)

## Verification
- [ ] Integration tests (macOS, mocked VoiceInput/VoiceOutput/Client + faked BLECentral): BLE down/up → idle→…→awaitingResponse; awaitTimedOut→idle then a down records again (F4 regression); captureStalled→exactly one restartCapture; bleDidDisconnect while recording → captureEnded→finalize; mediaKey recording does NOT suspend keep-alive
- [ ] `make test-mac-unit` green; `make test` no iOS regression

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #1, #2, #3, #4, #7, #8 (live behavior).

## Parallelization
After Gesture recognizer + Session reducer + VoiceInput capture-readiness + BLE conn executor.

title: Manual hardware validation of the overhauled macOS hands-free loop
description:
## Design Reference
@docs/design/macos-headset-loop-state-machine.md#acceptance-criteria + #verification-strategy

## Context
End-to-end confirmation on real hardware (B450-XT, firmware 2.6.4) that the reducer overhaul fixes the strand/misfire bugs and doesn't regress AirPods. Final gate for the epic. Tune the timer constants here.

## Requirements
- [ ] AC1: prompt with no spoken response → button records again within the await timeout (no strand)
- [ ] AC2: tap/double during speaking/awaitingResponse dismisses; HOLD barges in (interrupt + record)
- [ ] AC3: first capture after connect that yields zero buffers auto-restarts and captures (no re-press)
- [ ] AC4: hold = PTT (record/release-send); tap latches, second tap sends — no flicker
- [ ] AC5: reconnect via saved id after relaunch + out-of-range round-trip is fast (no advert wait); stale id never hangs
- [ ] AC7: AirPods path unaffected (play/pause start/stop; keep-alive not suspended on mediaKey)
- [ ] AC8: recording can't strand (recognizer silence / disconnect mid-record → finalizes)
- [ ] Tune + record final timer constants (captureGrace, awaitResponse, scanTick, connectWatchdog, discoveryWatchdog)

## Technical Approach
- Hardware test against the doc's acceptance criteria; capture logs (VoiceInput `capture summary firstAudio=…`, BlueParrottBLE, HeadsetRemote). Record validated firmware version.
- Dependencies: BLE conn executor (3x1.6), Headset session executor (3x1.7)

## Verification
- [ ] All AC #1–#8 pass on firmware 2.6.4 (AC6 = the automated suites, verified in the code tasks)

## Acceptance Criteria
Epic #1–#8 (end-to-end on hardware).

## Parallelization
None — final gate; requires both executors complete.
